review_notes: I read the whole file and the places that use these lemmas: TwoVariable/S.lean uses perm and add_const, and Series.lean has the continuation API. I also grepped the Carlson directory for @[simp] conventions. The file has no simp attributes. The perm, add_const and series add_const lemmas have lemma-shaped left-hand sides involving composition or a lambda with a free constant, so I did not recommend simp for them. I found no loop or competing-rule problem. The one issue is the right-hand side of regCarlsonSIntegral_zero, which is not in Mathlib's simp normal form. The finding is minor. regCarlsonSIntegral_zero has no other uses in the repository, so I could not check downstream effects. I did not run Lean.

findings.excerpt: regCarlsonSIntegral b (fun _ ↦ 0) = 1 / Gamma (∑ i, b i) := by
findings.problem: The right-hand side `1 / Gamma (∑ i, b i)` is not in Mathlib's simp normal form, because `one_div : 1 / a = a⁻¹` is a simp lemma. Any simp call that uses this identity, or any later simp call on its result, will turn the value into `(Gamma (∑ i, b i))⁻¹`. The stated form therefore never survives simp. This is why the proof has to go through `simpa`, which normalises both sides. The zero-variable special value is also not available to simp at all. Other zero and special-value lemmas in this library are tagged @[simp] (for example `regCarlsonLIntegral_empty`).
findings.proposed_change: State the value in simp-normal form: `regCarlsonSIntegral b (fun _ ↦ 0) = (Gamma (∑ i, b i))⁻¹`. If the `1 / Gamma` form is wanted for readers, keep it as a separate non-simp corollary. Consider @[simp] on the inverse form, since the side condition `b ∈ mvBetaConvergent` is a plain hypothesis that simp can discharge when it is in context. The proof should then close with `simpa [regCarlsonSIntegral] using ...` unchanged, or with a shorter `simp`.
findings.benefit: Users who simp with the zero-variable value get a stable normal form and need no extra `one_div` or `div_eq_inv` rewriting. The statement matches Mathlib's convention that `x⁻¹` is canonical over `1 / x`. The special value could be used by simp wherever the convergence hypothesis is available.
